DePIN’s Q3 numbers came from paying customers and real network usage, not token incentives.

Here are 9 milestones that mattered from July to September:

$GEOD: GEODNET earned $2.8M in Q3. It runs 22,000+ base stations and has 150+ enterprise customers.

$HNT: Helium’s 18,000+ active sites now serve about 1.5M people a day. One 23-hospital system moved 145TB of mobile traffic onto Helium in a single week.

HeliumOS: the new platform for carriers and large venues signed Affiniti Ventures, the company behind Noble Mobile and Helium Mobile, as its first customer.

$NOS: demand for RTX 4090 and 5090 compute outran supply. Nosana responded with host incentives and an MCP server for managing GPU deployments.

$NATIX: Valeo released VATIX, a driving world model family up to 9B parameters trained on up to 5,500 hours of driving video. NATIX is releasing the data in stages.

$AKT: Akash finalized its confidential computing spec, including confidential GPU workloads.

$LPT: Livepeer shipped Live Runner, a lightweight node that handles orchestrator discovery and payments for developers.

$RENDER: 80.7M frames rendered, about 5,600 nodes since launch and 1.53M RENDER burned by late September.

$WXM: WeatherXM has 9,500+ stations in 85+ countries. 5,900+ were active in August, and 4,300+ met its Synoptic Quality standard.

Revenue and enterprise adoption ($GEOD, $HNT) are stronger signals than cumulative network stats or burn counts.

Portrait mode launched 10 years ago today. 

I think it resonated with people because it didn’t feel digital. It felt analog. And this was likely because the inspiration behind its technique went all the way back to oil painting. Sometimes pure math isn’t enough; you need to combine it with insights from the liberal arts. 

If you recall Portrait mode shipped a month after the iPhone did. This was because this insight about oil painting took a while to figure out. 

Initially, Portrait mode was seen as a giant math problem. You’d do disparity calculations on the two sensors and output a depth map. The problem was this approach feels and looks digital; it feels fake. In areas without texture, it’s impossible to do this calculation. In areas with ultra fine detail, a lower resolution depth map leads to terrible transitions and a full resolution depth map takes forever to compute. One solution would be to reduce the amount of bokeh so the issues are not as obvious. But then you lose the whole point of the feature, which was to make it look like you had a large, wide-open lens.

The solution to this conundrum—the tradeoff between artifacts and the amount of blur— was quite elegant, but it took a while to stumble across. There’s a saying in painting that if you get the eyes right, nothing else matters. Inspired by this principle from oil painting, the idea was to make sure we never got the eyes wrong. We brought in a machine learning block to find the eyes, and draw a mask layer that protected them, then paired that with the disparity depth map. Counterintuitively, the solution was not to decrease the amount of blur, it was to increase it. The additional blur that we could add once the eyes were protected allowed us to hide the artifacts that were create by bad depth calculation. We let the ears go soft, let the nose go a bit soft. This is that wide open look that people loved, even if people didn’t realize that the ears going soft was why.

A lot of projects save the product for the announcement. This one did the opposite, and the last few months are pretty easy to line up.

July is when the captures and the USDC started landing on Base. August is when they said the Android app was live, and when they finally talked about the $9M, after the network was already running. September is the explorer, so you can check the Base attestations yourself, and then the agent door on Arc. One call, pay in USDC, no account.

This week they posted a CoinMarketCap verification ticket, 1467663. That's a ticket. I'm not calling it a listing until the page is actually there.

They also said, in their own words, that a bad capture doesn't reconstruct into a 3D scene and doesn't get paid. I'd still separate that from the harder checks. Device attestation and a real proof of the scene are not live yet. Their docs say so.

What's still sitting on "next" is iOS, from the Android post back in August, and $VAN. Neither has shipped. The thing I'm actually watching is whether the buyers keep paying, not the next logo.

Elon is right, and this thread proves it. Government isn't the antidote to big corporations. It's the biggest one of all, and the only one with a monopoly on legitimate violence.

That's why the dream of a world government is the most dangerous political project imaginable.

Think about it for two seconds. Concentrating the monopoly on legitimate violence in the hands of a small group of people, mostly unelected, convinced they know better than you what's good for you. And managing 8 billion humans the way you manage cattle.

History is brutally consistent on this: every time power gets concentrated, it ends up being abused. Every single time. The example above is one among thousands: state-backed researchers feeding radioactive oatmeal to disabled kids, and zero charges.

The only protection that has ever worked is diluting power. Checks and balances. Competing jurisdictions. The ability to leave. Private property.

Yet the European project as it's evolving, and the globalist project more broadly, are heading in exactly the opposite direction: more centralization, more rules decided far from citizens, more influence from NGOs nobody elected. It is literally a project to centralize the monopoly on legitimate violence.

Look at the UK today. People arrested for posts. Questioning the prevailing orthodoxy can cost you your freedom. Now imagine that model scaled to a continent, then to the planet, with nowhere left to run. That's not politics anymore, that's Orwell shipped to production.

If this trend isn't broken, we're heading into extremely dark times.

The alternative exists, and it's the light: private property, Milton Friedman economics, and companies obsessed with truth and efficiency rather than ideology. That's what Elon is building. SpaceX opening a massive share of its capital to retail investors instead of reserving it all for institutions. Companies that ship instead of promise.

Want less poverty? Support Elon. Want less totalitarianism tomorrow? Support Elon. Prefer an Orwellian world run by a corrupt hyper-class against its own people, like we've too often had for the past 40 or 50 years? Then go ahead: vote Democrat, vote left, and we'll get total chaos.

The choice has never been clearer.
